report.summary: Reviewed chunk 4 of 5 of daedalus/kairos/worktree.py. All enumerated claims are either kept or uncheckable; no broken code found in this window.
risks: worktree.py:841-... | medium | The docstring claims that _refuse_if_repo_adjacent on the resolved root covers all ancestor cases, but this is proven only by an external enumeration (216,225 shapes) not present in this chunk; a future change to that helper could invalidate the claim without visible breakage in this file. | Inspect the full implementation and tests of _refuse_if_repo_adjacent and any property-based tests covering those shapes.

worktree.py:... | medium | The claim that _remove_tree_no_follow is re-checking guarded ancestors on every open is unverifiable here; if the implementation skips a re-check, the race protection is weaker than documented. | Read the implementation of _remove_tree_no_follow and its tests.

worktree.py:... | medium | The claim that a retained allocation record can never re-authorize a delete depends on _require_allocated_worktree refusing non-existent paths; that check is present (step 5), but the allocation read happens before deletion and could be raced by a re-created path. The docstring does not discuss that race. | Review the full cleanup flow for TOCTOU between _require_allocated_worktree and _remove_tree_no_follow.

worktree.py:... | low | The comment claims that the order of checks makes each testable independently, but the proof that the escape check dominates the old root check is based on enumeration not shown here; a regression in the enumerated space would not surface in this chunk. | Review the test suite for the enumerated property tests.

handoff.purpose: Primary checkout identity checks, allocation proof, worktree creation, removal, and branch reap rationale.

symbols.name: _require_allocated_worktree
symbols.note: Validates that a path is an allocated worktree using lexical and no-follow checks; returns the unresolved path.

symbols.name: create_worktree
symbols.note: Creates a new git worktree after containment checks; records allocation and runs git worktree add.

symbols.name: cleanup_worktree
symbols.note: Removes an allocated worktree directory via _remove_tree_no_follow, runs git worktree prune, and retains the allocation record with a worktree_removed_ts.

symbols.name: reap_branches
symbols.note: Docstring only in this chunk; explains why branch deletion is separate from cleanup.

claims.text: the returned path is the UNRESOLVED one -- callers operate on exactly what was checked.
claims.why: The function returns `target` (the lexical path) at the end, not the resolved path.

claims.text: every check below is lexical or no-follow
claims.why: Checks use _key, _is_within, _is_reparse_point, _lexists, os.lstat, and _read_allocation; resolution is only used for an additional check and not for the final return.

claims.text: no symlink / junction anywhere from the worktree root down
claims.why: iterates _reach_chain(target) and raises if any component is a reparse point.

claims.text: a reparse point at any level can redirect everything below it
claims.why: The loop checks each component in the chain before resolution.

claims.text: only now is resolution trustworthy -- nothing at or below the root can redirect it
claims.why: Reparse point check on all components is performed before calling os.path.realpath.

claims.text: it must actually be there, as a real directory (no-follow)
claims.why: Uses _lexists and stat.S_ISDIR(os.lstat(target).st_mode).

claims.text: it must be something THIS manager allocated for THIS repo
claims.why: Calls _read_allocation(target) and raises if None.

claims.text: An allocation that cannot be contained is refused before anything is created
claims.why: The containment checks precede mkdir, require_storage, and _run_git.

claims.text: the allocation path in those is repo-adjacent to nothing, so the line below stays silent
claims.why: Depends on the implementation of _refuse_if_repo_adjacent and the enumerated shapes not present in this chunk.

claims.text: on a genuine ancestor chain with no reparse points, realpath is the identity map, so the resolved root is still that strict ancestor and `_refuse_if_repo_adjacent` fires on it
claims.why: The comment describes the behavior of the code: resolved_root is computed via realpath and then passed to _refuse_if_repo_adjacent.

claims.text: a single junction anywhere in DAEDALUS_WORKTREE_ROOT lands the entire worktree root inside the developer's checkout while every lexical check above passes
claims.why: The code resolves the root and then checks _refuse_if_repo_adjacent on the resolved root, which is designed to catch such junctions.

claims.text: The target must be PROVEN to be a worktree this manager allocated (see :meth:`_require_allocated_worktree`); anything else raises without removing a thing.
claims.why: cleanup_worktree calls _require_allocated_worktree before any removal.

claims.text: The removal itself is done here rather than by ``git worktree remove --force``, which follows reparse points planted inside the tree; ``git worktree prune`` then deregisters it.
claims.why: The code calls _remove_tree_no_follow and then _run_git('worktree', 'prune').

claims.text: The candidate BRANCH is deliberately left alone here -- see :meth:`reap_branches` for why deleting it in this call would be wrong.
claims.why: The code does not delete any branch; it only removes the directory and prunes.

claims.text: WorktreeRemovalRace: If a reparse point appeared above the removal while it was underway. The tree is PARTIALLY removed and that is what the exception says; it is deliberately not repaired.
claims.why: The exception is not raised in this chunk; it is raised inside _remove_tree_no_follow.

claims.text: A prune failure raises (RuntimeError from _run_git) rather than leaving a stale registration unreported.
claims.why: _run_git is documented to raise RuntimeError on failure; the code does not catch it around the prune call.

claims.text: The record is RETAINED, not discarded: it is now the only place that remembers which branch this worktree left behind and what its tip was at creation, which is what makes a later reap safe.
claims.why: The code writes the record with worktree_removed_ts instead of discarding it.

claims.text: The retained record can never re-authorise a delete -- cleanup refuses a path that does not exist, and this one no longer does.
claims.why: _require_allocated_worktree step 5 refuses non-existent paths.

claims.text: Tracked in memory as well as on disk: reap must not be steerable into deleting the branch of a worktree that is still LIVE just because a candidate wrote a `worktree_removed_ts` into its record.
claims.why: The code sets allocation['worktree_removed'] = True in memory.

claims.text: WHY THIS IS NOT PART OF ``cleanup_worktree``
claims.why: The reasoning is in the following lines, not included in this chunk.

observations.what: The docstring for _require_allocated_worktree claims that every check is lexical or no-follow, but step 4 uses os.path.realpath, which can follow symlinks. While the comment explains that reparse points are checked first, the docstring's absolute statement is slightly misleading.

In create_worktree, the containment check uses _refuse_if_repo_adjacent on the allocation path before the explicit escape check. The comment claims this order is deliberate and tested, but the proof relies on an external enumeration not present in this chunk.

The cleanup_worktree docstring claims that WorktreeRemovalRace is a RuntimeError, not an OSError, and passes through undisguised. This is not verifiable in this chunk because the exception is not raised here.

The comment in cleanup_worktree says that _remove_tree_no_follow re-checks guarded ancestors on every directory it opens. This is a claim about the helper's behavior that cannot be verified from this chunk.
